 The Premier League have issued a statement explaining why Noni Madueke was not sent off in Arsenal ’s win over Liverpool .
 As the huge Premier League showdown at Anfield entered its closing stages on Sunday afternoon, Madueke clashed with Alexis Mac Allister after the Liverpool midfielder had fouled Martin Odegaard .
 While the Gunners were awarded a free-kick on the edge of their own box, Mac Allister was not happy with the decision and had words with Odegaard - who was on the floor - and appeared to tap the Arsenal captain on the head.
 Madueke then came rushing over and leaned his head into Mac Allister as the two players came face-to-face, thus risking a potential red card for violent conduct.
 Interestingly, the Arsenal winger was already on a yellow card but referee Andy Madley did not punish Madueke, instead showing a yellow card to Mac Allister and Jurrien Timber.
 The Premier League’s match centre have now confirmed that Madueke avoided a red card because his action was not considered aggressive or violent.
 A statement reads: “The referee’s call of no violent conduct by Madueke on Mac Allister was checked and confirmed by VAR.
 “VAR: “All of the situations have been checked and cleared. There is some contact as Madueke and Mac Allister square-up. In my opinion, it's not forceful, not violent, not brutal”.”
 Alexis Mac Allister had words with Martin Odegaard which sparked a melee between Liverpool and Arsenal players AFP/Getty Gary Neville, who was on co-commentary duty for Sky Sports, slammed the Liverpool midfielder for going down far too easily and praised the VAR officials for not advising the referee to produce a red card.
 "Well done to VAR because they're recognised that Mac Alliser going down is embarrassing,” Neville said.
 "He said that, but in a posher way.”
